turns.t: Hiya, Kelly, I'm Dawn, the nurse. I'll weigh you and take your blood pressure first, then the doctor will go through your blood test. ~
Lovely. Oh, I've got so much to tell you, doctor, I've been reading all about it. ~
Weight 63 kilos, blood pressure 114 over 70, pulse 68, temperature 36.5.
Hello, Kelly. It's your coeliac follow-up. You've been on the gluten-free diet for six months now. How's it going?
Brilliant, honestly, once I got the hang of it. I've learned to read every label. I've been to a few restaurants. And my tummy's so much better. ~
And the bloating, and the loose stools you had before?
Gone. Well, almost. I haven't had a bad day in two months. No diarrhoea at all.
Any tummy pain, or other symptoms? ~
No, none. I feel a lot more energetic. ~
Are you taking anything at the moment?
A vitamin D tablet, 1000 units, once a day. And an iron tablet last year, but I've stopped.
Any other conditions?
An underactive thyroid, and a bit of eczema.
Do you drink alcohol?
Cider, or wine, at weekends. And gluten-free beer, I've discovered.
Good. Let me feel your tummy. Lie back.
Okay. ~
Your tummy is soft, no tenderness, and no bloating, and your skin looks healthy, no rash.
Her weight's up two kilos since the last visit, doctor. ~
That's good news, Dawn. Kelly, I've got your blood test from last week here. The antibody level has come down a lot, and your iron and vitamin B12 are normal. ~
So it's working. ~
Yes, it's responding very well to the diet. I'd say your coeliac disease is well controlled on the gluten-free diet.
Do I need another test? ~
I'd like to repeat the blood test in six months, to make sure the antibody stays down, and I'd like to arrange a bone density check, because coeliac can affect bones.
Okay. ~
Keep the diet strictly, even small amounts of gluten can keep the damage going. And watch cross-contamination, toasters and spreads.
I've got my own toaster. ~
That's the way. I'd also like you to see the dietitian once a year, and have the flu jab.
Will do. ~
I'll book your jab, if you like, Kelly. ~
Yes, please. ~
If your symptoms come back, or you lose weight, get a rash with blisters, or become very tired, come back sooner.
I will. Thanks, doctor. Thanks, Dawn. ~
